issue.title: Instagram using generated tracking parameters?
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I noticed recently that I've been seeing Instagram links from friends where there's a clear tracking parameter, but instead of the usual `igshid`, `igsh`, or `igsi` name, the parameter has some random-looking four character name. In the past couple days alone I've seen `psln`, `srtk`, and `exln`. Earlier I've also observed `stkn` and `vrfl`. The value for each is always 12-13 bytes encoded as base64.

I didn't see these parameters in the [specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt) list or anyone else reporting this phenomenon, so I wanted to give a head up that they may be encoding/randomizing their tracking parameters. Given that Instagram is a huge platform (and Meta a notorious tracker), I thought you'd want to know.

### Proposed solution

This is more of a heads up than a specific feature request. The way to address this depends highly on the pattern in the parameters. It may not be worth overcomplicating the matching rules. If it's always 4 lowercase letters, though, it looks like you could use a regex to match them. If that's too broad, you can restrict it to certain paths (I've only seen these on `/reel/` urls).

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
A little update: it's clearly not randomized every time; I keep seeing the same set recurring. These are all the ones I've seen so far:
```
"stkn", "vrfl", "exln", "psln", "srtk", "cplk", "mdxt", "xtok", "rpxt", "dlrf"
```

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Indeterminate — Reproduced the blank gtaservers.org homepage in the prepared current extension with the reporter's settings and identified the culprit from the engine's applied-rule log:⁠ the generic Base-filter hide rule `##.home-ads` matches the site's own page container `<body class="home-ads home-ads--rails">` and blanks the entire page. The fix `gtaservers.org#@#.home-ads` restored the whole site in the experiment (11.5k-px page, header, hero, sidebar, cards, no ads returning), but the bound review still flagged one empty in-feed ad panel, so the rule remains unverified and is reported for a human.

- Main content column, immediately below the 'NOPIXEL V' featured server card (below the LIVE / 143k viewers row) and above the green '1' ranked server card — Empty rounded rectangular block that renders with only a flat grey-purple fill:⁠ no image, no video, no text, no creative, no label and no interactive control inside it. It occupies the space of a full-width content/ad panel in the server list column while every neighbouring card renders normally, i.e. a region where content should render that is visibly absent.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported anti-adblock wall ("An ad blocker is preventing this page from loading") did not appear:⁠ on two loads of the esportstales.com article the full page rendered with no overlay (structured full-page vision:⁠ symptom absent, 0 instances), because the site's detecting request ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js is already answered by the existing Base-filter redirect-to-noop rule, so no __adblocker state is set and the html-load.com / error-report.com wall never loads. Recommend closing as not reproduced; no new rule is needed.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's policy blocks German anti-adblock walls, paywalls and first-party ads; this is an English-language site's anti-adblock interstitial and the captured page/network evidence shows the detector script, so policy does not forbid rule generation here. Rule generation is allowed, but the captured live evidence shows the reported defect absent under the repository baseline, so no rule is written and the report is recommended for closing.

### Issue URL (Ads) [NSFW] [https://kissjav.li/video/852679/%EC%B9%BC%EB%8B%A8%EB%B0%9C%EB%85%80-%EB%94%B0%EB%A8%B9%EC%9D%80-%EB%82%A0/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fkissjav.li%2Fvideo%2F852679%2F%25EC%25B9%25BC%25EB%258B%25A8%25EB%25B0%259C%25EB%2585%2580-%25EB%2594%25B0%25EB%25A8%25B9%25EC%259D%2580-%25EB%2582%25A0%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > > **URL:** `https://kissjav.li/video/852679/%EC%B9%BC%EB%8B%A8%EB%B0%9C%EB%85%80-%EB%94%B0%EB%A8%B9%EC%9D%80-%EB%82%A0/` > > #### 1. What is the problem? > > **Delayed Pop-under / Pop-up Advertisements** > > - After approximately 20 seconds on the page, clicking anywhere triggers an unsolicited pop-up or pop-under advertisement through `window.open()`. > - The first redirect points to `tsyndicate.com` (TrafficStars direct link). > - After another 15 seconds, a subsequent click triggers a second advertisement redirecting to `ethnicexpressions.org`. > - These advertisements are triggered by user interactions with the page rather than intentional clicks on advertisements. > > **Right-Click and Developer Tools Blocked** > > - The website intercepts `contextmenu` events to disable the browser's right-click menu. > - Keyboard shortcuts such as `F12`, `Ctrl+Shift+I/J/C`, `Ctrl+U`, and `Ctrl+S` are intercepted through `keydown` event listeners. > - These restrictions interfere with normal browser functionality and make inspecting the injected advertising scripts more difficult. > > #### 2. Steps to Reproduce > > 1. Navigate to the affected video page: > `https://kissjav.li/video/852679/%EC%B9%BC%EB%8B%A8%EB%B0%9C%EB%85%80-%EB%94%B0%EB%A8%B9%EC%9D%80-%EB%82%A0/` > 2. Wait at least 20 seconds without interacting with the page. > 3. Click anywhere on the video player or page background. > 4. Observe a new advertising tab or window opening, redirecting to `tsyndicate.com`. > 5. Wait approximately another 15 seconds and click again. > 6. Observe a second advertising redirect to `ethnicexpressions.org`. > 7. Right-click anywhere on the page or press `F12`. > 8. Observe that the context menu or developer tools shortcut is blocked. > > #### 3. Technical Analysis > > The page executes an inline JavaScript snippet that intercepts pointer events and tracks pop-up state using `sessionStorage`. > > **Relevant JavaScript:** > > ```javascript > const URL_1ST = "https://tsyndicate.com/api/v1/direct/bf57abd2ecb34326a34db1a8e88e6f30"; > const URL_2ND = "https://ethnicexpressions.org/4/4ffb29d9a3e14249b993653a8c94060a"; > > const SESSION_KEY = 'v_pop_' + PAGE_ID; > > // First advertisement after 20 seconds > if (timeElapsed >= 20000) { > triggerPop(URL_1ST, 1); > } > > // User interaction listeners > document.addEventListener('pointerup', handleUserAction, true); > document.addEventListener('click', handleUserAction, true); > ``` > > **Additional Advertising-Related Elements:** > > ```html > <meta > name="popads-verification-3515163" > value="de608b382a48b19d1c2c7878dbb92ea0" > /> > > <script src="//alfalfaemployeeresource.com/on.js"></script> > ``` > > **Browser Interaction Restrictions:** > > - `contextmenu` event interception prevents normal right-click interactions. > - `keydown` event interception blocks developer tools and browser shortcuts. > - Both restrictions are implemented through JavaScript event listeners. > > #### 4. Suggested Filter Rules > > **Block advertising networks and unwanted scripts:** > > ```adblock > ||tsyndicate.com^$domain=kissjav.li > ||ethnicexpressions.org^$domain=kissjav.li > ||alfalfaemployeeresource.com^$domain=kissjav.li > ||cdnhop.com/static/js/video.instant.message.js$domain=kissjav.li > ``` > > **Prevent unwanted pop-ups:** > > ```adblock > kissjav.li#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open') > ``` > > **Restore right-click and browser keyboard shortcuts:** > > ```adblock > kissjav.li#%#//scriptlet('prevent-addEventListener', 'contextmenu') > kissjav.li#%#//scriptlet('prevent-addEventListener', 'keydown') > ``` > > **Optional: Investigate session-based pop-up tracking** > > The script uses a dynamically generated `sessionStorage` key based on `PAGE_ID`: > > ```javascript > const SESSION_KEY = 'v_pop_' + PAGE_ID; > ``` > > A static storage rule targeting `v_pop_` may not match the dynamically generated key. A more targeted scriptlet or inline-script filtering approach may be necessary. > > #### 5. Expected Behavior > > - Clicking the video player or page background should not trigger unsolicited advertising windows. > - Delayed advertising redirects should be blocked without disrupting normal video playback. > - Standard browser functionality, including the right-click context menu and developer tools shortcuts, should remain accessible. > - Advertising countermeasures should not interfere with legitimate page interactions. ### [NSFW] Screenshots [Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/9g8fyy1kl7ok408c8cksg4gks804ocwbkygokftr7k.jpg?nc=1) ### System configuration | Information | Value | |-------------|-------| AdGuard product: | AdGuard for Mac v2.20.2.2629 release System version: | `版本27.2（版號26B123）` Browser: | Chrome Filters: | **Ad blocking:**

What is the problem? > > **Delayed Pop-under / Pop-up Advertisements** > > - After approximately 20 seconds on the page, clicking anywhere triggers an unsolicited pop-up or pop-under advertisement through `window.open()`. > - The first redirect points to `tsyndicate.com` (TrafficStars direct link). > - After another 15 seconds, a subsequent click triggers a second advertisement redirecting to `ethnicexpressions.org`. > - These advertisements are triggered by user interactions with the page rather than intentional clicks on advertisements. > > **Right-Click and Developer Tools Blocked** > > - The website intercepts `contextmenu` events to disable the browser's right-click menu. > - Keyboard shortcuts such as `F12`, `Ctrl+Shift+I/J/C`, `Ctrl+U`, and `Ctrl+S` are intercepted through `keydown` event listeners. > - These restrictions interfere with normal browser functionality and make inspecting the injected advertising scripts more difficult. > > #### 2. Steps to Reproduce > > 1. Navigate to the affected video page: > `https://kissjav.li/video/852679/%EC%B9%BC%EB%8B%A8%EB%B0%9C%EB%85%80-%EB%94%B0%EB%A8%B9%EC%9D%80-%EB%82%A0/` > 2. Wait at least 20 seconds without interacting with the page. > 3. Click anywhere on the video player or page background. > 4. Observe a new advertising tab or window opening, redirecting to `tsyndicate.com`. > 5. Wait approximately another 15 seconds and click again. > 6. Observe a second advertising redirect to `ethnicexpressions.org`. > 7. Right-click anywhere on the page or press `F12`. > 8. Observe that the context menu or developer tools shortcut is blocked. > > #### 3. Technical Analysis > > The page executes an inline JavaScript snippet that intercepts pointer events and tracks pop-up state using `sessionStorage`. > > **Relevant JavaScript:** > > ```javascript > const URL_1ST = "https://tsyndicate.com/api/v1/direct/bf57abd2ecb34326a34db1a8e88e6f30"; > const URL_2ND = "https://ethnicexpressions.org/4/4ffb29d9a3e14249b993653a8c94060a"; > > const SESSION_KEY = 'v_pop_' + PAGE_ID; > > // First advertisement after 20 seconds > if (timeElapsed >= 20000) { > triggerPop(URL_1ST, 1); > } > > // User interaction listeners > document.addEventListener('pointerup', handleUserAction, true); > document.addEventListener('click', handleUserAction, true); > ``` > > **Additional Advertising-Related Elements:** > > ```html > <meta > name="popads-verification-3515163" > value="de608b382a48b19d1c2c7878dbb92ea0" > /> > > <script src="//alfalfaemployeeresource.com/on.js"></script> > ``` > > **Browser Interaction Restrictions:** > > - `contextmenu` event interception prevents normal right-click interactions. > - `keydown` event interception blocks developer tools and browser shortcuts. > - Both restrictions are implemented through JavaScript event listeners. > > #### 4. A more targeted scriptlet or inline-script filtering approach may be necessary. > > #### 5. The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

On kolaygelsin.com the arrow-marked element is the homepage hero carousel, which serves the company's own promotional slides from its own CDN (no third-party ad host at all), so filter policy forbids a rule for the site's own advertising; the cookie-consent panel also visible in the same screenshot is already hidden by two existing rules in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. No new rule is needed.

## Policy rationale

Filter policy, ad blocking filters:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked." The element the reporter's arrow marks is the homepage hero carousel (.banner_root__NfM3r inside <⁠main data-testid="welcome"⁠>) whose only creative is a promotional image served from the company's own CDN (sendeocdn.blob.core.windows.net, asset name prefixed "kolaygelsin-") advertising its own delivery service — first-party advertising, so no rule; recommend closing. Run instruction policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The other candidate reading of the screenshot, the cookie-consent panel, requires no new rule either:⁠ it is already hidden by the existing rules kolaygelsin.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠class*="CookieConsentBanner_container__"]⁠ and kolaygelsin.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠class^="Box_container___"]⁠[⁠data-testid="box-container"]⁠:⁠has(⁠> img[⁠src="/assets/icons/cookie.svg"]⁠) in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, and the element is display:⁠none in the loaded filtered page.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on www⁠.nuerburgring.de/events/categories/automotive/dtm is the inline footer newsletter subscription block (NEWSLETTER heading, "Deine E-Mail" input, arrow submit button) served in the page's own HTML, with no network request behind it and no existing filter rule covering it. The domain-scoped cosmetic rule nuerburgring.de#⁠#⁠.activities__col:⁠has(#⁠subscribe_form) was verified in the AdGuard Browser Extension baseline:⁠ the block was visible before, hidden after, page integrity intact, no layout residue and no remaining instances. ## Rule `nuerburgring.de##.activities__col:has(#subscribe_form)` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No run-instruction policy rule closes this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no ad-blocker detection, and interact_page produced no gate or overlay). The reported element is a newsletter signup block, which the filter policy places in the scope of the AdGuard Popups filter ('Popups and forms for subscribing to news, promotions, and various events'). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c719a228ffe16c3d3a1ca9c5a9c2a2757e8a18aa/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41189996179 Automated analysis against filters at `c719a22`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — huavod.net serves third-party ad banners:⁠ a wide slot (.hr-slot-box) directly below the 热映排行 heading — the banner in the reporter's screenshot — plus sponsored hero-carousel slides (.slide-time-img3--ad gambling/dating creatives) and their 赞助一/赞助二 links. One domain-scoped element-hiding rule covering those placements was verified in the reporter's filter profile:⁠ ads gone, a normal drama slide in the hero, page integrity intact. ## Rule `huavod.net##.hr-slot-box, .slide-time-bj:has(.slide-time-img3--ad), .slide-nav-list a.pagination-block[href^="https://"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The banners are third-party advertising (external advertisers 467.hk, wg6u.com, 192.253.235.247:⁠8888), not the site's own promotion, so the 'site's own advertising' exclusion does not apply. No paywall or anti-adblock gate is involved; the page shows no anti-adblock notice. The rule is cosmetic element hiding with no performance impact, anchored on the site template's own ad markup and placed in the filter that already holds this site's rules. ## Place in the list [ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/26b0593402f3f272f63f592b04ad268bde7c8b07/ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 247](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/26b0593402f3f272f63f592b04ad268bde7c8b07/ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L247). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41198757992 Automated analysis against filters at `26b0593`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Hi everyone! I'm Turtle, the owner of [adblock.turtlecute.org](adblock.turtlecute.org).

I understand that your goal is to block ads, and I respect that. I maintain the largest adblock test website and i do it entirely in my free time, and like everyone else, I need to make a living.

I know banners can be annoying, but unfortunately, they're the only way I can keep the website online. Sponsorships and donations haven't been a viable option, and users generally aren't willing to pay for an adblock testing tool.

I've even set up a bot that notifies me whenever your blocking rules change, allowing me to adjust the website's banner within about five minutes. But realistically, this creates an endless cat-and-mouse game that wastes both your time and mine.

**That's why I'm commenting this issue: I'd genuinely like to find a solution that works for both sides.**

I believe we could spend our time on much more productive things rather than constantly trying to outsmart each other. I'm open to discussing possible compromises that respect your goals while allowing me to keep providing this free service.

Feel free to reach out in the comments below or contact me directly at **turtlecute...at...proton [dot] me**.

Thanks for your time, and I hope we can find some common ground!

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — subanalyzer.com shows a first-party cookie consent card ("Cookies and analytics", "Necessary only"/"Accept all") fixed at the lower-right that AdGuard Cookie Notices did not hide. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for the banner's own data-cookie-banner attribute was verified in the CLI-filtered experiment:⁠ banner hidden, symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no residue. ## Rule `subanalyzer.com##section[data-cookie-banner="true"]` ## Policy rationale The report is an in-scope annoyance (cookie/consent notice) that the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is designed to block, per the filter policy's 'AdGuard Cookie Notices filter' section. None of the closing rules apply:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing page. The reported product is AdGuard Mini for Mac (Safari), a website-filtering app, so the fix belongs in the shared filter lists; the rule is plain #⁠#⁠ element hiding, which Safari-converted content blockers support. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/26b0593402f3f272f63f592b04ad268bde7c8b07/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"d40ffce7eb37995b279a722a7bb4c2763f7a97c736e685cd68ed17d517257508"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — taraftarium24bjk26.com is a missing mirror of a site family that TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt already fixes for taraftarium24bjk17.com and taraftarium24tvizle.com; one domain-scoped hiding rule removed all 122 main-document betting ad anchors (page-skin, marquee strips, in-list rows, banners) with page integrity intact. Validation stayed rejected only because a betting CTA is rendered inside the cross-origin player frame (player.taraftarium24bjk26.com), which no available tool can inspect, so the complete fix is extending that family's four rules with this domain.

## Still visible after the rule

- Video player panel — poster bottom banner — Betting call-to-action banner reading 'MAÇ ÖNCESİ BAHİSİNİ AL! HEMEN TIKLA!' overlaid on the stream poster inside the video player panel.
- Left viewport edge — full-height page-skin column — Large blank reserved side column at the left edge, full height and visibly wider than ordinary section spacing; no creative, label, frame, or placeholder block is visible, but it matches the page-skin ad-column footprint.
- Right viewport edge — full-height page-skin column — Large blank reserved side column at the right edge, full height and visibly wider than ordinary section spacing; no creative, label, frame, or placeholder block is visible, but it matches the page-skin ad-column footprint.
- Left viewport edge, full-height page-skin ad column — Large full-height blank reserved side column at the left viewport edge, matching the page-skin advertising footprint; no creative, ad label, frame or placeholder block is visible in this overview.
- Right viewport edge, full-height page-skin ad column — Large full-height blank reserved side column at the right viewport edge, matching the page-skin advertising footprint; no creative, ad label, frame or placeholder block is visible in this overview.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Missing information

- No tool can read a cross-origin subdomain frame's DOM (player.taraftarium24bjk26.com): The remaining reported advertising ("MAÇ ÖNCESİ BAHİSİNİ AL! HEMEN TIKLA!" betting CTA over the stream poster) is rendered inside the iframe https:⁠//player.taraftarium24bjk26.com/ch?id=b1. That text is absent from the main document (verified:⁠ documentElement.innerHTML and body.innerText contain no 'MAÇ ÖNCESİ', 'HEMEN TIKLA' or 'YAYIN BAŞLIYOR'). open_page refuses navigation off the configured issue origin, so the player document cannot be opened; get_dom, evaluate_js, inspect_ad_slots and inspect_page_state only expose the main frame. The proxy's own request log shows cosmetic injection is started for that frame (`local.adguard.org/?...type=content-script&dmn=player.taraftarium24bjk26.com&...css=3`), so the element is reachable in principle by a domain-scoped rule, but no tool in this run can reveal its selector, and guessing one would be fabrication. With the run limited to one filter rule, this prevents a verified single-rule outcome even though a main-document rule removing all 122 ad anchors (page-skin, both marquee strips, in-list rows, header/footer banners) validated with intact page integrity and no damage.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — golbettv6.com shows a full-viewport promo popup (DIV.popup-overlay with the Ryan Babel coupon card and Kapat button) that dims and gates the home page. The lists already carry a plain element-hiding line for that overlay which the live filtered baseline still renders, so I validated a CSS-injection rule with display:⁠none !important, which hides the popup with page integrity intact. ## Rule `golbettv6.com#$#.popup-overlay { display: none !important; }` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules do not cover this report:⁠ the page shows no paywall and no anti-adblock wall (an 'Anti-adblock'/'Annoyance' label is not evidence, and the page itself shows a promotional modal, not a blocker-detection message). The reported element is an obstructive in-page promo popup that dims and gates the whole page until the blue KAPAT button is clicked, which is exactly what the Popups annoyances filter is defined to block; it is not an ad slot served by a third party and no ad network request renders it (network log:⁠ 0 blocked, no ad-vendor host). Repository practice confirms the category:⁠ TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt already carries golbettv6.com#⁠#⁠.popup-overlay and golbettv6.com#⁠#⁠.bnr for this same site, so no 'first-party advertising:⁠ recommend closing' rule applies here. ## Place in the list [TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e5a0f240b023c9be3de43da4b328336e1958be85/TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 4691](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e5a0f240b023c9be3de43da4b328336e1958be85/TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt#L4691). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
